# diabetes-algo

This is the code and configuration for `diabetes-algo`, which is an R reusable action for the OpenSAFELY framework.

The action implements two diabetes adjudication algorithms. Users choose which one to run with the `--algorithm` argument:

| `--algorithm` | Algorithm | Input variables | Diabetes types (variable `cat_diabetes`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Eastwood` (default) | Eastwood algorithm (Figure 1 below) | 21 | GDM, T2DM, T1DM, DM_other, DM_unlikely |
| `DDSC` | DDSC algorithm (see [DDSC_Algorithm_Results_V2_0.pdf](DDSC_Algorithm_Results_V2_0.pdf)) | 14 | T2DM, T1DM, DM_other, DM_NOS, DM_unlikely |

The value is case-insensitive (e.g. `--algorithm=ddsc` also works). If `--algorithm` is not provided, the action runs the Eastwood algorithm, so existing projects keep working unchanged.
The two algorithms need different input variables. The arguments for each are listed in the sections below.

## Choosing the algorithm

The algorithm can be chosen at the command line:

```yaml
diabetes_algo:
  run: diabetes-algo:[version] --algorithm=DDSC --df_input=input.arrow
```

or with an `algorithm` key in the `config:`:

```yaml
diabetes_algo:
  run: diabetes-algo:[version]
  config:
      algorithm: DDSC
      df_input: input.arrow
```

## Eastwood algorithm (`--algorithm=Eastwood`, default)

The Eastwood pipeline:

- Loads and double-checks 21 input variables
- Runs the diabetes adjudication algorithm (Figure 1 below) to define the following Diabetes types:
-   Gestational, Type 2, Type 1, Other, Unlikely (variable 'cat_diabetes': GDM, T2DM, T1DM, DM_other, DM_unlikely)
- Besides the categorical type variable, it provides the diagnosis date for each type. The default choice of diagnosis date sources for each type is:
-   gestationaldm_date: First date from GDM clinical codes
-   t2dm_date: First date from T1DM clinical codes, T2DM clinical codes, unspecific diabetes clinical codes, and diabetes medication codes
-   t1dm_date: First date from T1DM clinical codes, T2DM clinical codes, unspecific diabetes clinical codes, and diabetes medication codes
-   otherdm_date: First date from T1DM clinical codes, T2DM clinical codes, unspecific diabetes clinical codes, diabetes medication codes, and diabetes-specific procedure codes
- Version 0.0.10 allows users to change the above-mentioned default choice of diagnosis date sources and define their own sources, see args gestationaldm_date_sources, t1dm_date_sources, t2dm_date_sources, otherdm_date_sources
- The output dataset is saved to `output/Eastwood/`

## DDSC algorithm (`--algorithm=DDSC`)

The DDSC pipeline:

- Loads and double-checks 14 input variables
- Runs the DDSC diabetes adjudication algorithm (see [DDSC_Algorithm_Results_V2_0.pdf](DDSC_Algorithm_Results_V2_0.pdf)) to define the following Diabetes types:
-   Type 2, Type 1, Other, Not otherwise specified (NOS), Unlikely (variable 'cat_diabetes': T2DM, T1DM, DM_other, DM_NOS, DM_unlikely)
-   Unlike the Eastwood algorithm, DDSC has no separate gestational diabetes category, and it distinguishes diabetes of other specified aetiology (DM_other) from diabetes not otherwise specified (DM_NOS)
- Besides the categorical type variable, it provides one diagnosis date (variable 'diabetes_diag_date'): the first date of any diabetes diagnosis code (T1DM, T2DM, Other, NOS) or of the first of two consecutive high HbA1c readings, if more than a year before the first diabetes code. It is missing for DM_unlikely
- The output dataset is saved to `output/DDSC/`

## Usage

The input variables/arguments/options to the action are specified using the flags style (i.e., `--argname=argvalue`).
Below, you find a detailed description of each input variable for each algorithm, including examples for codelists to use when defining these variables in the OpenSAFELY dataset definition.
IMPORTANT: The used codelists here are just examples. Users have to double-check these. Important is to adhere to the specified source (primary or secondary care) where these codelists should come from.
Copy-paste the argument names into your yaml and map them to your input variable names.
Example dataset definitions that define all input variables can be found here:

- Eastwood (21 input variables): [analysis/dataset_definition_Eastwood.py](https://github.com/opensafely-actions/diabetes-algo/blob/main/analysis/dataset_definition_Eastwood.py)
- DDSC (14 input variables): [analysis/dataset_definition_DDSC.py](https://github.com/opensafely-actions/diabetes-algo/blob/main/analysis/dataset_definition_DDSC.py)

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Taken from
# https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/077-wrap-output.Rmd
library(knitr)
hook_output <- knit_hooks$get("output")
knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  # this hook is used only when the linewidth option is not NULL
  if (!is.null(n <- options$linewidth)) {
    x <- knitr:::split_lines(x)
    # any lines wider than n should be wrapped
    if (any(nchar(x) > n)) x <- strwrap(x, width = n)
    x <- paste(x, collapse = "\n")
  }
  hook_output(x, options)
})

# Prints the help of a data_process script: evaluates the lines from
# `option_list <- list(` up to (and including) the OptionParser(...) call,
# i.e. everything before `opt <- parse_args(...)`
library(optparse)
print_action_help <- function(file) {
  lines <- readLines(file)
  start <- grep("^option_list <- list\\(", lines)
  end <- grep("^opt <- parse_args", lines) - 1
  env <- new.env()
  eval(parse(text = lines[start:end]), envir = env)
  optparse::print_help(env$opt_parser)
}
```

### Eastwood arguments

```{r, echo=FALSE, comment = '', linewidth=80}
print_action_help("analysis/Eastwood/data_process_Eastwood.R")
```

### DDSC arguments

```{r, echo=FALSE, comment = '', linewidth=80}
print_action_help("analysis/DDSC/data_process_DDSC.R")
```

## Example YAML

This action can be specified in the `project.yaml` with its options at their default values as follows,
where you should replace `[version]` with the latest tag from
[here](https://github.com/opensafely-actions/diabetes-algo/tags), e.g., `v0.0.1`.
Note that no space is allowed between `diabetes-algo:` and `[version]`.
This action can be run specifying input arguments as follows (in YAML ">" indicates to treat the subsequent nested lines as a single line).

Eastwood:

```yaml
generate_dataset_Eastwood:
    run: ehrql:v1 generate-dataset analysis/dataset_definition_Eastwood.py --output output/input_Eastwood.arrow
    outputs:
      highly_sensitive:
        dataset: output/input_Eastwood.arrow

diabetes_algo_Eastwood:
  run: >
    diabetes-algo:[version]
      --algorithm=Eastwood
      --df_input=input_Eastwood.arrow
      --birth_date=your_dob_date_variable
      --tmp_t1dm_primarycare_date=your_t1dm_from_primcare_date_variable
      --tmp_max_hba1c_mmol_mol_num=your_max_hba1c_num_variable
      --## more arguments
      --df_output=data_processed.csv.gz #or data_processed.rds
  needs:
  - generate_dataset_Eastwood
  outputs:
    highly_sensitive:
      csv.gz: output/Eastwood/data_processed.csv.gz #or data_processed.rds
```

DDSC:

```yaml
generate_dataset_DDSC:
    run: ehrql:v1 generate-dataset analysis/dataset_definition_DDSC.py --output output/input_DDSC.arrow
    outputs:
      highly_sensitive:
        dataset: output/input_DDSC.arrow

diabetes_algo_DDSC:
  run: >
    diabetes-algo:[version]
      --algorithm=DDSC
      --df_input=input_DDSC.arrow
      --birth_date=your_dob_date_variable
      --last_observable_date=your_last_observable_date_variable
      --nosdm_date=your_diabetes_nos_date_variable
      --## more arguments
      --df_output=data_processed.csv.gz #or data_processed.rds
  needs:
  - generate_dataset_DDSC
  outputs:
    highly_sensitive:
      csv.gz: output/DDSC/data_processed.csv.gz #or data_processed.rds
```

Alternatively, the input arguments (including `algorithm`) can also be specified using a `config:` key in the YAML as follows.
Input arguments specified in the config overwrite those specified at the command line.

```yaml
diabetes_algo_via_config:
  run: diabetes-algo:[version]
  config:
      algorithm: DDSC
      df_input: input_DDSC.arrow
      birth_date: your_dob_date_variable
      nosdm_date: your_diabetes_nos_date_variable
      ## more arguments
      df_output: data_processed.csv.gz #or data_processed.rds
  needs:
  - generate_dataset_DDSC
  outputs:
    highly_sensitive:
      csv.gz: output/DDSC/data_processed.csv.gz #or data_processed.rds
```

For more information about reusable actions see [here](https://docs.opensafely.org/actions-reusable/).

# About the OpenSAFELY framework

The OpenSAFELY framework is a Trusted Research Environment (TRE) for electronic
health records research in the NHS, with a focus on public accountability and
research quality.

Read more at [OpenSAFELY.org](https://opensafely.org).
